speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) whether the Ministry has studied the importance of economic connectedness through cross-class interaction between families of low and high socio-economic status in uplifting children from lower-income families; and (b) what specific changes in policies have been adopted to take into account such economic connectedness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: As more in our society progress, the Government endeavours for society to continue progressing together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In our public policy design, we also consider how best to promote social interaction, including among different income groups of our society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In our residential estates, we have actively sought to foster a good mix of socio-economic groups.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We work to ensure that our schools remain open and accessible to students from different backgrounds.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In addition, there are opportunities for students from different schools to interact with one another and with the larger community, such as through co-curricular activities (CCAs), values-in-action projects and cluster-based activities and competitions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We have also sought to increase the social capital of those from lower-income backgrounds through volunteering and mentoring opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Many community partners and volunteers from diverse backgrounds provide services and programmes to lower-income families under our "Many Helping Hands" approach.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Youths, including those from lower-income backgrounds, can be connected to mentors to build their tenacity, soft skills and knowledge.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The close bonds fostered allow for useful information and opportunities to be shared with youths and families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: While the Government can shape diverse environments and channels for interactions between different socio-economic groups, all of us must play our part to reach across the lines of status and class.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In particular, those who are more privileged and better-connected should realise that their success in life is also because of the kind of society we have built over time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: So, we hope they will always step forward to contribute their time, networks and effort to uplift those with less.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We need a whole-of-society effort to help lower-income families as they work towards stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think he mentioned there is some peer-to-peer social mixing in CCAs and then, peer-to-mentor social mixing in some of the programmes through ComLink.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I ask whether the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) is rolling out new programmes that will have peer-to-peer social mixing within the community?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, making friends with the same age group and not just the peer-to-mentor.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I ask whether MSF can conduct a similar study in Singapore to see whether it holds true that social mixing is the most important factor so that we can tailor our programmes and have a more targeted impact on the ground?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In today's programmes – not within the ambit of MSF but me wearing my Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) hat – we do have programmes where peer-to-peer interaction across different socio-economic groups is already taking place.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: That is where the interaction across socio-economic groups already takes place.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I cite this as one of many other examples across the different agencies' programmes and services that we provide.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I also want to draw some reference from the study which points to a finding, such as the stickiness with respect to how members of each socio-economic status group are having a resistance to mixing with members from a different socio-economic status group.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: A finding, such as this, is somewhat confirmatory of what we know intuitively – we do not really need additional research in order to confirm or conclude as such.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: But I do note the Member's suggestion for such studies to be conducted in the local context, so that it can better appreciate the nuances or the different nuances.
